{'content': 'The Xiao family returned home this afternoon to pack up family photographs, ancient coins and calligraphy left behind by their grandparents, as well as some clothing. However, due to limited time and the fact that the unit had already had its water and electricity cut off, they were unable to sort through all their belongings and will return next week to tidy up again. In the past, the Xiao family had installed CCTV outside their home. After the land resumption operation, when the Xiao family returned home, they found that the relevant CCTV had been covered with plastic bags.'}

{'content': 'The Lands Department recently replied twice, pointing out that it was only when the department arranged to hand over the structures to the Civil Engineering and Development Department earlier this year that Mr. Xiao suddenly moved into the squatter hut. They also stated that he is a public housing tenant and therefore does not meet the rehousing eligibility criteria. The department emphasized that it, together with a social work team, has been in contact with Mr. Xiao since the beginning of the year.'}

{'content': 'The Xiao family previously told "集誌社" (Jizhixiang) that after their father-in-law passed away in 2019, her husband and other siblings inherited the land title through estate administration, and they signed off on the land compensation two years ago, but have yet to receive the payment. The Xiao family continued to refute the claims, stating that during the Cha Kwo Ling village fire in 2016, her husband was already at the scene escaping with their mother and five pets, and that there was even media coverage and filming of him. They are dissatisfied with the Lands Department\'s claim that her husband moved in mid-way.'}

{'content': "Another accusation from the Xiao family is that they have not received the compensation since signing the land compensation documents. The Lands Department previously confirmed that part of the land is government land and part is private land. The former owner of the private land has accepted the government's land compensation offer, but the relevant documents are still pending signing by the former owner's representative lawyer. The department also stated that it will disburse the land compensation as soon as possible after receiving the duly signed documents."}
